messages:
maria: Heads-up: observed a 15-25% p95 regression on decode for long-context requests after the kernel-autopick change merged yesterday. Repros locally on dedicated infra. Profiling dump below.

dennis: Which model/config and is this prefill or decode path?

maria: gptx-13b int8 quantized. Prefill ~128 tokens, then decode ~3800 tokens. Regression is almost entirely in the decode loop.

oliver: The kernel-selector autotuner was changed to prefer the fused matmul kernels for sequences >512 based on throughput tests. Could be that fused path is suboptimal for our KV cache layout during long streaming decode.

tanya: Can you paste the sampling output / nvprof lines? Any big memcpy or kernel variance?

maria: Pasted sample (trimmed):
```
[profile] decode_step     1.32 ms  (matmul_gemm_fused)
[profile] kv_read        0.48 ms  (gpu memcpy)
[profile] attention_kv   0.75 ms  (reshape/copy)
[profile] matmul_old     0.62 ms  (baseline matmul)
-- decode loop dominated by matmul_gemm_fused + kv_read with high variance
```

jess: That looks like the fused kernel increases contiguous memory assumptions and triggers larger memcpy for KV. If prefill created a fragmented KV layout (small prefills across batches) the fused path pays a heavy memcopy penalty.

dennis: We should check how the autotuner is computing sequence-length stats during calibration. If it's using mean it can be skewed by many short requests. Use p90/p95 buckets instead.

maria: Quick experiment: toggling the prefer_fused_kernels_for_long_seq flag back to false returns decode p95 to baseline. So kernel pick is the culprit.

oliver: Hypothesis: autotuner uses avg_seq_len for kernel selection and doesn't consider decode-only runtime tail. For streaming decode after a short prefill, effective decode sequence is large and our KV layout differs. Need to make autotuner aware of tail percentiles or separate prefill/decode signals.

tanya: Short-term mitigations: 1) Split runtime selection into short-decode and long-decode kernel sets. 2) Add a cheap preflight to inspect request headers (expected decode length) and pick kernel accordingly. 3) Consider adjusting KV cache layout for long-decode flows to be contiguous to avoid repeated memcpy.

jess: :100: vote for 1+2. Preflight should be very cheap (use declared max_tokens or last-token hint) and we should add a runtime flag to force old kernel set for canary.

maria: I'll open a PR with: a runtime flag `kernel_selection_mode`, emitted diagnostics (kernel_choice, seq_bucket, kv_memcpy_ms), and an autotune job that records p50/p95 across seq buckets.

dennis: Also add a perf regression test to our suite: synthetic stim with prefill=128 decode=3800, assert decode p95 <= baseline * 1.05.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled for `kernel-bucket-fix` to 5% traffic starting 2024-06-10 18:00 UTC.

oliver: One more note: batching heuristics currently sometimes mix short and long requests into the same batch which amplifies the memcpy penalty. We should dispatch batch buckets earlier (by predicted decode length) so kernels see homogeneous sequence lengths.

maria: Filing issue and will link PR: https://redwood.atlassian/browse/INF-4829. I will attachPerfJob results + baseline artifacts.

tanya: I'll help update the perf harness to synthesize different KV layouts and validate memcpy cost.

jess: :thumbsup: Thanks everyone — keep updates here and ping if you need cluster access for experiments.
